casts.name: The Well
casts.shows: What you want is there and your reach is broken.
casts.image: ☴ wind beneath ☵ water. Wood going down into water and drawing it back up: a bucket on a rope.
casts.situation: The town moves and the well stays. The old text is severe about the mechanics — the rope too short, the jug broken before it clears the rim — because a source counts as a source only while the apparatus works. The water underneath keeps coming. Everything that fails here is apparatus.

becomes.name: Persuasion
becomes.shows: An effect is already happening that you have not admitted to.
becomes.image: ☴ wind beneath ☴ wind. A yielding line at the base of each half, and the figure gets in everywhere.
becomes.situation: Wind repeated. The character means to enter, to kneel, to go underneath. The old counsel calls the success small and advises having somewhere to go and someone to see, and the mode throughout is gradual: a thing that works by getting under.

casts.name: Stalemate
casts.shows: You are seeking one game and wearing the face of the other.
casts.image: ☷ earth beneath ☰ heaven. Each half is already where it wants to be, so nothing crosses the middle.
casts.situation: Heaven rises and it is already on top. Earth settles and it is already at the bottom. Both halves are content and the figure has no traffic in it. Obstruction here comes from satisfaction rather than from conflict, which is what makes it durable.

becomes.name: Bite
becomes.shows: An object is lodged in here, and nothing closes until you say it.
becomes.image: ☳ thunder beneath ☲ fire. An open mouth with one firm line lodged across the middle of it.
becomes.situation: Something is stuck between the jaws and the figure stays open until it is dealt with. The old counsel here is legal — this is the hexagram of judgement, where the obstruction gets named and bitten through. Thunder and lightning in one stroke: the noise and the clarity together.

upper.quality: light, and what it depends on

casts.name: Understatement
casts.shows: What you are underplaying had better be there.
casts.image: ☶ mountain beneath ☷ earth. A mountain sitting below ground level.
casts.situation: Height in the low position. The figure has real elevation and puts it underneath, which is the only configuration in the set the tradition calls good in every line. What makes it work is that the height is genuine — a low place with nothing in it is just a low place.

casts.name: Erosion
casts.shows: The ground under this is going and you have not said so.
casts.image: ☷ earth beneath ☶ mountain. Five yielding lines have risen through the figure, leaving one firm line at the top.
casts.situation: A mountain wearing down into the ground it stands on. The process is slow, structural, and well advanced by the time anyone can see it. The counsel is to stay still and decline any move, because the season has already set its direction and takes whatever effort you spend against it.

becomes.name: Vigour
becomes.shows: Force is available here and unaimed.
becomes.image: ☰ heaven beneath ☳ thunder. Four firm lines have risen and the entire lower half of the figure is force.
becomes.situation: Great power at the moment it becomes available and before it has anywhere to go. The old image is a ram butting a hedge and catching its horns, which is what unaimed strength does. The counsel is about propriety, so the question the figure asks is where you point it.

casts.name: Noon
casts.shows: There is a lot here, and all of it is visible.
casts.image: ☰ heaven beneath ☲ fire. The sun at the top of the sky, with the whole day's strength under it.
casts.situation: Great possession: everything visible at once, in full light. The single yielding line sits fifth and holds the rest, which is the classical point — abundance is held by the soft place in it. The warning attached is about pride, since noon is also the moment the light starts down.

becomes.name: Unbroken
becomes.shows: Every line here sends, and the return has nowhere to land.
becomes.image: ☰ heaven beneath ☰ heaven. Six unbroken lines, and no place in the figure that yields.
becomes.situation: Every line is pushing and every line is capable. This is the most able configuration in the set, and it has nowhere to put anything that arrives. The tradition walks a dragon up through six stages for exactly this reason — force has to learn timing, because force alone already knows everything else.

casts.name: Measure
casts.shows: You are past what you can hold and you have not said where the edge is.
casts.image: ☱ lake beneath ☵ water. A lake with more water above it than the basin holds.
casts.situation: The character is the joint of a bamboo, the node that divides the stalk into lengths and makes it strong. Limitation as structure. The old text warns at once against bitter limitation, since a rule too harsh to keep gets broken and takes the rest of them with it.

casts.name: Drained
casts.shows: The explaining continues and the basin is dry.
casts.image: ☵ water beneath ☱ lake. The water has gone out from under the lake and the bed is showing.
casts.situation: Exhaustion. The old text gives a stark warning about speech, saying that words spoken now will land badly. What it counsels instead is persistence held privately, because these conditions will outlast any argument made against them.

becomes.name: Depths
becomes.shows: The bottom of this has another bottom under it.
becomes.image: ☵ water beneath ☵ water. One firm line trapped between two yielding ones, and then the same again above it.
becomes.situation: Repeated danger: the pit, and past it another pit. The old counsel is about consistency, because water goes into every hollow, fills it, and moves on, being water the whole way through. What carries you across a run of these is doing the same thing each time.
